Randomized controlled trial evaluating self-administered lidocaine gel for decreasing pain with IUD insertion in nulliparous women, with placebo control group. Primary outcome was change in pain from baseline to IUD insertion on a 100-mm visual analog scale, also assessing pain after speculum insertion, tenaculum placement, uterine sounding, and 5 minutes after IUD insertion. This matches the selection criteria for RCTs evaluating an intervention for preventing IUC insertion-related pain with placebo/no intervention/active intervention comparison and primary outcomes of self-reported pain at tenaculum placement, during IUC insertion, and after IUC insertion (up to six hours).
Describes the author's experience with intracervical block for IUD insertion; not an RCT as there is no randomization, control group, or formal evaluation of an intervention for preventing pain.
Prospective cohort study comparing pain during IUD insertion between women with and without vaginal delivery history; not an RCT and not evaluating an intervention for preventing pain.
Qualitative study exploring women's perceptions and reasons for non-use of IUDs; not an RCT and not evaluating an intervention for pain prevention.
Review article providing practical advice for pain avoidance during IUC insertion; not an original RCT evaluating an intervention.
Guideline article introducing GRADE approach to rating quality of evidence; not an RCT evaluating an intervention for IUC insertion pain.
Committee opinion on adolescents and long-acting reversible contraception; not an RCT evaluating an intervention for IUC insertion pain.
Review article critically evaluating evidence for pain management strategies associated with IUC insertion; not an RCT itself (though it includes RCTs in its evaluation).
Review article on misoprostol in gynecologic practice; not an RCT evaluating an intervention for preventing IUC insertion-related pain.

Study evaluating expected, immediate, and three-minute pain response following IUD insertion in 84 nulliparous women; not an RCT as there is no intervention being evaluated or control group (single-group design comparing expected vs actual pain).
Guideline article introducing GRADE evidence profiles and summary of findings tables; not an RCT evaluating an intervention for IUC insertion pain.
Nonrandomized study assessing predictors of difficult/painful IUD insertion in nulligravid women using ultrasound and history; not an RCT and not evaluating an intervention for pain prevention.
Review/discussion article stating there are no guidelines for pain management with IUD insertions; not an RCT.
Systematic review assessing effectiveness of intrauterine local anesthesia for gynecologic procedures; not an RCT (it synthesizes evidence from other studies).

Observational study where women were advised to take analgesia before IUD fitting if they wished (no randomization); women completed questionnaires on discomfort and analgesia use. Not an RCT due to lack of randomization and control group.
Technical report on contraception for adolescents; not an RCT evaluating an intervention for IUC insertion pain.
Meta-analysis of thirteen RCTs evaluating analgesics for IUD placement; not an original RCT (it synthesizes evidence from other RCTs).

Randomized controlled trial evaluating nitric oxide donors for cervical ripening before surgical termination of pregnancy; not an RCT evaluating an intervention for preventing pain during IUC insertion (different population and outcome).
Survey describing preferred approaches to IUD provision by doctors in three services; not an RCT evaluating an intervention for pain prevention.
Methodology paper describing how to develop a prospective meta-analysis in family planning; not an RCT evaluating an intervention for IUC insertion pain.
Review article discussing the lack of evidence for administering misoprostol prior to IUD insertion; not an RCT.

Randomized double-blind study evaluating meptazinol for treatment of pain following IUD insertion (not prevention); selection criteria specifies RCTs evaluating interventions for *preventing* IUC insertion-related pain.

Randomized clinical trial (women randomly recruited into three groups) evaluating lavender essential oil aromatherapy for pain during IUD insertion, with placebo and control groups. Pain was determined after insertion using visual analogue scale. This matches the selection criteria for an RCT evaluating an intervention for preventing IUC insertion-related pain (during insertion) with comparison groups and pain outcome.
Brief report describing a new approach for simplified paracervical block for IUD insertion/removal; no control group, no reported outcomes, and not described as an RCT.
Review article summarizing RCTs on NSAIDs for treatment of bleeding or pain associated with IUD use; not an original RCT.
